clue.text: Added gold bar roughly

blocks.note: more means added or extra
or is the heraldic word for gold
bar as a preposition means except, as does less ('five bar two')

explanation.surface: A jeweller adds a bar of gold to the hoard, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a noun for the gold, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for approximately, just as roughly is.

clue.text: Endless row after problem about fabric

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a problem is read backwards
without an end, so the final letter of the word for a row is dropped
after sends the shortened row second, behind the piece for the problem

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A never-ending quarrel follows some dispute over cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it is a line; 'after' puts the shortened line behind the turned problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Muslin is a lightweight cotton cloth, so it is an example of a fabric.

clue.text: Bitter herb dock packed makes you apologetic

indicators.note: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail, so the last letter of the following word goes

blocks.note: rue is a bitter-tasting herb
packed means full

explanation.surface: Eating a bitter herb that fills you up leaves you feeling sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' looks like another plant after the herb, but it is the instruction to cut a letter off.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means feeling or showing regret, which is how someone apologetic behaves.

clue.text: Vulgar promises to pay after a lot of port gets on shabby clothes

indicators.note: a lot of means not all, so the port's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: Ostend is a Belgian ferry port
tat is cheap, shabby goods or clothing
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A sailor on shore leave, scruffily dressed, runs up debts at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: The IOUs come last because they come 'after' the docked port and the tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentatious means showy and pretentious, a display in poor taste, which is a sense of vulgar.

clue.text: Fat boy cramming in last of burger

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is wanted
cramming in means stuffing inside, so the boy holds the letter

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
the final letter of burger

explanation.surface: A greedy boy stuffs down the rest of his burger.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat used in cooking, so it is a kind of fat.

clue.text: One in bed is game to continue for a while!

blocks.note: snap is a card game
to drag on is to continue tediously for some time

explanation.surface: A sleepy quip that a game in bed keeps going a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' is a flower bed, not a place to sleep; the plant is also the name of a Christmas parlour game, adding a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden flower, so it is something growing in a flower bed.

clue.text: After a month, returned and got a hole in one

indicators.note: after places the letter behind the month that follows it in the clue
returned means sent back, so the letters so far are read from the end

blocks.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer, a month after starting, goes back out and scores a hole in one.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as A after a month, giving DEC then A, and the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to ace a hole is to sink the ball with a single stroke.

clue.text: Carriage circles a bay tree

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so the carriage encloses what follows

blocks.note: a calash is a light low-wheeled carriage with a folding hood
taken as written
B is a dictionary abbreviation for bay

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage drives round a bay tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay tree' reads as one thing, but bay is the letter and tree alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The calabash is a tropical American tree whose gourd-like fruit is dried for vessels.

clue.text: Doctor amazed with pi and another possible number

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are falsified into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor is astonished at pi and some other possible number.
explanation.walkthrough: With pi in the surface, number reads as a figure; here it is something that numbs, a pun crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: Diazepam is a sedative, so it dulls feeling and could be called a numb-er, a thing that numbs.

clue.text: Loud senator going around with tin

indicators.note: going around suggests moving about, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy senator goes about carrying a tin, perhaps collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian describes a voice that is very powerful, after Stentor, the herald in Homer.

clue.text: Circus performer is to escape during broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, not read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to flee is to escape

explanation.surface: A circus act makes a break for it during a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: A flea circus is a sideshow of performing fleas, which makes the insect a circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleas were the stars of the old flea circus, a miniature show of insects pulling tiny carts.

clue.text: Does it provide a better way to play "Oranges and Lemons"?

definitions.text: Does it provide a better way to play "Oranges and Lemons"?

blocks.clueFragment: Does it provide a better way to play "Oranges and Lemons"?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about performing the nursery rhyme or children's singing game
setter's reading: oranges and lemons are symbols on the reels of a gambling machine in a pub or arcade

explanation.walkthrough: Oranges and Lemons is a traditional English nursery rhyme and playground game; the clue reimagines it as the symbols you hope to line up on a one-armed bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaming machine whose reels show fruit symbols is named for them, so playing it means playing oranges and lemons.

clue.text: Reptile disfiguring canal's central parts

indicators.note: only the middle letters of each of the two words are wanted

blocks.note: the middle three letters of disfiguring
the middle three letters of canal

explanation.surface: A reptile in a canal is spoiling the waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disfiguring' looks like an anagram signal, but it is fodder for the middle-letters instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, so it is a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Fuss by pub about the French sweet

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a pub is read backwards

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
a bar is a pub
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A row at a pub over a French dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like a noun for a dessert; it is the adjective meaning lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means charming and delightful, the sense of sweet used of babies and puppies.

clue.text: Be training around a ship

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to train aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, so it is one kind of ship.

clue.text: A lot of water replacing cider, as it's being consumed by non-drinkers

indicators.note: replacing means putting back in a different place, so these letters are reordered
something consumed goes inside, so the reworked letters sit within what follows

blocks.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members do not drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: Teetotallers swap the cider for plenty of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is held inside the two As, which split to open and close the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and the Balkans, a great body of water.

clue.text: Key on a dead mushroom

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
taken as written
the late means the dead, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: A key sits on a dead mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' looks like a noun, a fungus; it is the verb meaning to grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to expand fast, and to escalate is to increase rapidly in scale.

clue.text: Paper reviewed green comic strip

indicators.note: reviewed is read here as viewed back, so the word for a paper runs backwards

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a green is a grassy area, a field

explanation.surface: A newspaper's critic reviews a new, green comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' suggests a critic's verdict, but it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: Garfield is the long-running cartoon about a lazy lasagne-loving cat, a famous newspaper strip.

clue.text: School head comes round with toiletry

indicators.note: to come round something is to surround it, so the first pair encloses what follows

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for school
with means having, as in 'a house with a garden'
a head is the froth or foam on a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A headteacher makes the rounds carrying a toiletry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School head' reads as a headteacher, but it is two pieces; together they surround the word for with.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaving foam is a lather put on the face before a razor, a standard bathroom product.

clue.text: Susan regularly found behind joke book

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: to josh is to joke or tease
the second and fourth letters of Susan

explanation.surface: Susan keeps turning up behind a joke book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joke book' reads as one item, but book alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua is the sixth book of the Old Testament, so it is a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Something rude to do is eating very fast

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside it

blocks.note: staring at people is rude
V is an abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: It is bad manners to eat very fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as quickly; it is the verb meaning to go without food, so eating misleads twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to go without food, which is what fasting means.

clue.text: American female — elegant and wealthy

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for American
F is an abbreviation for female
fluent means smooth and graceful, as in elegant prose

explanation.surface: A stylish and rich American woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means having plenty of money, a near synonym of rich.

clue.text: Stop pretence about a possible alternative to sweetheart

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for pretence surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: an act is a pretence, as in 'putting on an act'
cos and sweetheart are both kinds of lettuce

explanation.surface: Stop pretending you might have another sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' suggests a lover, but it is a lettuce variety, and cos is another.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to stop and approach them boldly in the street.

clue.text: Fit date seen outside Uni

indicators.note: something seen outside wraps around what follows

blocks.note: an age is a date or period
U is an abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student's fit date is spotted outside the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is British slang for attractive, but here it is a noun meaning a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fever with shivering, and a fit of shivering is a bout of it.

clue.text: A place to hide port

blocks.note: taken as written
a den is a hideaway or lair

explanation.surface: A port would be a fine place to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Master chess player is heard to be big-headed beaky type

indicators.note: is heard means the name is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a king is a ruler or master
Bobby Fischer was the American world chess champion

explanation.surface: A chess master is said to be arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big-headed' looks like arrogance; it describes a bird with a large head and long bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a brightly coloured bird with a large head and a long dagger-like beak.

clue.text: Twist and slip when taking top off

indicators.note: removing the top of a down entry means the first letter goes

blocks.note: a teddy is a one-piece undergarment, a kind of slip

explanation.surface: Taking off a top, someone twists and slips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking top off' suits undressing, and the slip being undressed is the garment itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl or whirl of water, a twisting current.

clue.text: Slow month on railroad, with terminally tiresome speed

indicators.note: terminally means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
the El is an elevated railroad in American cities such as Chicago
the final letter of tiresome
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A slow, tedious month spent on the railroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To decelerate is to reduce speed, the verb sense of slow.
